_comment: Pins RFC-MACP-0001 Section 7.6 items 1, 2 and 3. The fixture's own Decision session is opened implicitly by the harness, as in every fixture, and stays Open. Each message is a SessionStart for a DIFFERENT session (envelope.session_id), and each is otherwise valid so it fails on exactly one obligation. There is deliberately no uppercase-UUID case: item 2's UUID and base64url forms are non-exhaustive examples of formats that meet RFC-MACP-0004 Section 11.2, not a normative format list, so no specific well-formed format is required to be rejected.
description: SessionStart acceptance obligations: short session_id, unsupported macp_version, policy bound to another mode.

policy.description: Decision-mode policy that case (c) binds to a Task-mode SessionStart.

messages._comment: (a) RFC-MACP-0001 Section 7.6 item 2: 's1' is two characters, and no format could carry the entropy RFC-MACP-0004 Section 11.2 requires in that length.
(b) RFC-MACP-0001 Section 7.6 item 1: macp_version '2.0' is not a supported version. The session_id is a lowercase UUID v4.
(c) RFC-MACP-0001 Section 7.6 item 3 and RFC-MACP-0012 Section 6.1 step 5: a Task-mode SessionStart binds the registered Decision-mode policy. The session_id is a lowercase UUID v4.
